title: Run restart reconciliation from the daemon boot path
description:
Objective: give `reconcileOnRestart` its first production caller, so restarting the real daemon durably writes its classification records instead of only doing so when a test asks. GAP B of the Foundation self-host canary (task-97554aa4293e40eab56c0b642e18513a).

MEASURED GAP at HEAD e881141, re-verified independently of worker-d6220bc6's earlier reading and unchanged since:
- `reconcileOnRestart` is defined at `apps/daemon/src/recovery/restart-reconciliation.ts:235` with signature `(store: SqliteEventStore, request: RestartReconciliationRequest) => RestartReconciliationResult`. It classifies each in-flight attempt via `classifyCrash`, commits one record per attempt, and returns `{ok:false, code:"EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT", layer:"DURABLE_STORE"}` on a conflict.
- COMPLETE CALLER SET, production: NONE. The callers are `recovery/continuation-test-harness.ts:6,73` (a test harness by name and by fact, itself imported only by continuation-binding.test.ts and continuation-service.test.ts), `restart-reconciliation.test.ts:9,27,28,133,216`, `restart-reconciliation-idempotence.test.ts:7,55,56,82,83,84`, and one doc comment at recovery-succession-contract.ts:97.
- `startDaemon` (`apps/daemon/src/daemon-entry.ts:162`) does `resolveDependencies` -> mint CSRF token -> `startControlRoomListener` -> freeze and return. No reconciliation sweep anywhere on the boot path.
- The two recovery capabilities that ARE wired are different ones and do not classify in-flight attempts: `runRecoveryCompleteCommand` via daemon-command-registry.ts (completion digest) and `createRestorePort` via daemon-store-dependencies.ts:16 (restore/quiesce).

Deliverable, two edges:
1. A reconciliation sweep on the durable boot path — in `startDaemon` or the store-dependency composition root — that reads the in-flight attempts, calls `reconcileOnRestart` once, and lets the result decide whether the daemon continues. Fail closed: an `EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT` or an unreadable attempt set refuses startup with a stable code and layer; it never boots as if reconciliation had succeeded.
2. The continuation command exposed through the registry, so `evaluateContinuationCommandBytes` (`recovery/continuation-service.ts:143`) is reachable by an authenticated command rather than only by a test.

NOT in scope: changing `reconcileOnRestart`'s classification logic or its record shape; the pinned Claude spawn (GAP A, owned by the ff589 -> 32eddfd3 -> 75ee4a84 -> 6cbff010 chain plus task-d7b352e1); the coordination command kind (GAP C, its own task); the canary journey itself.

Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/daemon-entry.ts (or daemon-store-dependencies.ts, whichever the composition root turns out to be), apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts, and their tests. Do NOT edit restart-reconciliation.ts or continuation-service.ts — they are complete and this task is the consumer edge.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test — read the OUTPUT count line, not the exit code. Daemon gates are red at baseline from foreign slices; apply the path-attributed baseline over the owned paths.
definitionOfDone: `grep -rn "reconcileOnRestart" --include=*.ts apps | grep -v '\.test\.' | grep -v test-harness` returns a PRODUCTION call site on the boot path in addition to its own definition — the production caller count was zero before this task.

A test drives the real boot path with in-flight attempts present and asserts the durable store afterwards holds one classification record per attempt, read back from the store rather than from the function's return value.

A reconciliation that cannot complete refuses startup with a stable code AND layer — `EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT` at `DURABLE_STORE` for a conflict, and a distinct pinned code for an unreadable attempt set — and the daemon does NOT become ready; a test asserts the daemon is not listening after such a refusal.

Reconciliation runs exactly ONCE per start: a test starting the daemon twice asserts the second start does not duplicate records for already-classified attempts, exercising the idempotence `restart-reconciliation-idempotence.test.ts` already pins at the pure layer.

`evaluateContinuationCommandBytes` is reachable through an authenticated registry command; a test sends the command and asserts a real receipt, and an unauthenticated or malformed send is refused with its exact code and layer.

A mutation removing the boot-path call turns a NAMED test red, and a mutation making the refusal path continue to listen turns a different NAMED test red — proving both the wiring and the fail-closed direction are load-bearing.

`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` run with exit codes captured separately; the test leg prints a nonzero Test Files/Tests count line, and the HEAD-minus-merge-base failing-path delta intersected with the owned paths is EMPTY.
taskRails: This is a CONSUMER EDGE task. Do not modify `reconcileOnRestart`, `classifyCrash`, the reconciliation record shape, or `evaluateContinuationCommandBytes` — they are complete and separately tested. If one genuinely cannot be composed as written, report blocked rather than editing it.

Do NOT route the sweep through `continuation-test-harness.ts`. It is a test harness by name and by fact; composing production through it would make the harness production authority and leave the gap exactly where it is.

Fail closed: a reconciliation that conflicts, or an attempt set that cannot be read, refuses startup with a stable code and layer. A daemon that boots ready after a failed sweep is the defect this task exists to prevent.
Real SqliteEventStore in tests, opened per test and closed in a `finally` on every exit path — a held handle kills the vitest worker.
Preserve foreign work; commit only the explicit owned paths by pathspec — never a bare `git commit`, never `git add -A`.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED — the boot sweep, driven against a REAL SqliteEventStore opened per test and closed in a `finally` on every exit path (a held handle kills the vitest worker). Write these before wiring; each must FAIL against current HEAD, since `startDaemon` runs no sweep today.
(a) IN-FLIGHT ATTEMPTS ARE CLASSIFIED. Seed attempts the enumerator will return, start the daemon, and assert the durable store afterwards holds ONE reconciliation record per attempt — read back from the store, not from `reconcileOnRestart`'s return value.
(b) THE SWEEP REFUSES STARTUP. `reconcileOnRestart` answers `{ok:false, code:"EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT", layer:"DURABLE_STORE"}` on a conflict, and `InFlightAttemptSweep` can refuse in its own right. For each, assert the daemon does NOT become ready — not merely that a refusal was returned. Assert the listener is not accepting connections afterwards; a daemon that boots ready after a failed sweep is the defect this task exists to prevent, and a verdict-only assertion cannot see it.
(c) BOTH REFUSAL SOURCES ARE DISTINGUISHABLE. The enumerator's refusal and the reconciler's refusal are different facts — one means "I could not read what was in flight", the other "I could not durably record the classification". Assert the exact code AND layer for each, and assert they are not collapsed into one entry code.
(d) EXACTLY ONCE PER START. Start, stop, start again, and assert the second start does not duplicate records for already-classified attempts. `restart-reconciliation-idempotence.test.ts` already pins idempotence at the pure layer, so this case exercises the WIRING rather than re-deriving that property.
(e) A CLEAN BOOT IS UNAFFECTED. With no in-flight attempts, the daemon starts normally and writes no reconciliation records — the control that stops the suite passing by refusing everything.

- (b/c) reconciler code+layer -> `expected { …(5) } to strictly equal { …(4) }` — a STARTED daemon (5 keys) where a 4-key refusal belongs.

- (b) readiness after an unreadable set -> `expected true to be false`.
- (c) distinguishability -> `expected undefined not to be undefined` — no code/layer/source exists yet to be distinct.

- composition -> `expected 'undefined' to be 'function'` — the production provider exposes no reconciliation port.
- (e) clean boot -> PASSES at HEAD, correctly. It is the CONTROL that stops the suite passing by refusing everything, so it must be green before and after.

SCOPE NOTE, deliberate and disclosed: the plan named `apps/daemon/src/daemon-entry.test.ts` as the test file. I put these in a NEW sibling, `apps/daemon/src/daemon-entry-reconciliation.test.ts`, and touched daemon-entry.test.ts not at all. daemon-entry.test.ts is 181 lines and holds the process/CSRF/lifecycle suite with no durable store anywhere in it; adding ~300 lines of store-backed boot tests would push it past the 250 target toward the 400 cap and mix two fixtures. The repo already splits this way — daemon-entry-document-dossier.test.ts is the precedent. Same suite, same `src` glob, so the gate runs it.

FIXTURE ORDERING FOUND THE HARD WAY, worth the next agent's time: seeding the store BEFORE `createStoreDependencies` makes every provider throw `GENESIS_RECOVERY_BINDING_FAILED: GENESIS_INSTALL_REFUSED (RECOVERY_INITIAL_INSTALL_HISTORY_PRESENT)` (daemon-store-dependencies.ts:107). `installInitialRecoveryBinding` refuses a store that already has history, so a seeded-then-opened store is one no daemon can own. The provider is now built first and the attempts are seeded through a second short-lived handle after it — which is also the honest order, since a real crash writes its reservations through a daemon that already installed genesis. My first run failed 8/8 on that throw rather than on the assertions; the reds quoted above are from the corrected run.

NOTHING IS STUBBED. Attempts are seeded through `commitFoundationPhase`, the writer the dispatch path uses. Both refusals are provoked by real durable conditions: RECORDED-with-no-RESERVED for the enumerator (`FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_DISPATCH_SUSPECT`), and a foreign-command-kind write on `reconciliationAggregateId(attemptRef)` for the reconciler — `readStored` counts only `reconciliation.decide` decisions, so that write advances the aggregate past the expectedVersion the reconciler presents and produces a genuine `EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT`. Records are read back with `readReconciliationRecords`, never from a return value. A stub port answering a hand-typed code would have satisfied the DoD text while proving nothing.

READINESS IS ASSERTED BY CONNECTING (`net.connect` to the requested port, resolving true/false), in two tests whose ONLY assertion is that boolean. Drill 2's red therefore lands on readiness, not on a changed code. Every seed count is asserted before it is used (`inFlightRefs(storePath, n)` fails loudly on a sweep that produced nothing), so a fixture that silently generated zero cases cannot pass.

implementationPlan.description:
WIRE THE SWEEP. In `startDaemon` (daemon-entry.ts:162), after `resolveDependencies` succeeds and BEFORE `startControlRoomListener`: call `readInFlightFoundationAttempts`, handle its refusal arm, then call `reconcileOnRestart(store, request)` with the real output and handle its refusal arm. A refusal from either returns `refuseEntry(...)` with a stable code at `DAEMON_ENTRY_LAYER`, and the listener never starts.
BUILD THE REQUEST FROM BOOT FACTS, NOT FROM A CALLER. `RestartReconciliationRequest` is `{attempts, correlationId, decidedAt, principalId, projectId}`. The attempts come from the enumerator; project and principal come from the resolved dependencies; correlationId and decidedAt are minted here as server facts. Nothing in `DaemonStartOptions` may supply any of them — a start option that could set the principal would let a caller attribute a reconciliation to someone else.
DO NOT MODIFY the producers: `restart-reconciliation.ts` and `in-flight-attempts.ts` are complete and separately tested, and `continuation-service.ts` is untouched by this step. If either genuinely cannot be composed as written, report blocked rather than editing it.
DO NOT ROUTE THROUGH `continuation-test-harness.ts`. It is a test harness by name and by fact — it was `reconcileOnRestart`'s only non-test caller before the enumerator landed, and composing production through it would leave the gap exactly where it is while looking closed.
LINE BUDGET: `daemon-entry.ts` is at 206 of a 250 target and 400 hard cap, so there is real room — but measure with `grep -c ''` after editing (PowerShell `Measure-Object -Line` undercounts). If the sweep plus its refusal handling would push past 250, put the sweep in a sibling module with its own one-line LF bridge and keep `startDaemon` a thin call.

implementationPlan.description:
EXPOSE THE CONTINUATION COMMAND — the second edge this task owns. `evaluateContinuationCommandBytes` (recovery/continuation-service.ts:143) has no authenticated caller; expose it through `daemon-command-registry.ts` so a continuation decision can be made by command rather than only by a test.
FIRST, MEASURE WHETHER A KIND EXISTS. `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` (packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:85) is a FROZEN union, and `runtime-envelope.ts:142` refuses any envelope whose `commandKind` fails `isCommandKind` BEFORE `http-adapter.ts:196` reads the registry — one seam, decode first. So a brand-new kind would be unreachable, and the union is closed for M5 by human decision recorded 11:54Z (no `RuntimeCommandKind` expansion, no client regeneration).
The union already contains `recovery.reconcile_external`, `recovery.inspect_external` and `reconciliation.decide` — and `RESTART_RECONCILIATION_COMMAND_KIND` is literally `"reconciliation.decide"` (restart-reconciliation.ts:23). Check whether one of those is the intended carrier before concluding anything. If a suitable kind is in the union, register the handler behind it with its own capability, payload allow-list and family entry, following the shape `RECOVERY_COMPLETION_COMMAND_KIND` already uses as a singleton kind.
IF NO EXISTING KIND HONESTLY CARRIES IT, do not mint one and do not fake the edge: say so in the completion and report that half of DoD 5 as blocked on a contracts-expansion prerequisite, exactly as the coordination surface was. Half an honest task beats a registry entry nothing can reach.
Either way, assert: an authenticated command produces a real receipt; an unauthenticated or malformed send refuses with its exact code and layer; and the payload allow-list refuses a field carrying a server fact rather than silently overwriting it.
implementationPlan.note:
CONTINUATION COMMAND EXPOSED — an EXISTING union kind carries it, so nothing is blocked and no kind was minted. `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 6 passed (6)` on the new suite, and daemon-command-registry.test.ts stays green at 113 passed.

THE CARRIER WAS ALREADY DECIDED BY THE PRODUCER, which is better than any of the three candidates step 4 listed. `continuation-contracts.ts:32-34` declares `CONTINUATION_COMMAND_KINDS = ["work.resume"] as const satisfies readonly RuntimeCommandKind[]` — so the kind is a member of the frozen `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` union, checked at compile time by that `satisfies`, and `continuation-service.ts:72` already COMMITS under it. `work.resume` is present in the union at runtime-vocabulary.ts. It was simply never registered: `PAYLOAD_KEYS` had no entry, so `buildCommandRegistry` never saw it and `isCommandKind` admitted an envelope the registry then had nothing for. No union expansion, no client regeneration, nothing for the 11:54Z M5 freeze to bite. `reconciliation.decide` would have been the wrong answer — it is `RESTART_RECONCILIATION_COMMAND_KIND`, the kind reconciliation ROWS are written under, and registering a second meaning there would have put continuation bytes in the set `readStored` scans.

NEW FILE apps/daemon/src/recovery/continuation-command.ts (90 lines) + its `.js` bridge, rather than 40 more lines in daemon-command-registry.ts. That file was already 320 lines at HEAD — over the 250 target before I touched it — so the edge lives in its own module and the registry gained 26 lines to 346, inside the 400 cap. `continuation-service.ts` and `continuation-contracts.ts` are byte-untouched, per the consumer-edge rail.

THE ALLOW-LIST IS EXACTLY TWO KEYS, and that is forced rather than chosen. `parseContinuationRequest` (continuation-contracts.ts:207-222) demands EXACTLY eight keys — attemptRef, correlationId, decidedAt, kind, principalId, projectId, schemaVersion, successorRef — and six of those are server facts. So `payloadKeys` is `["attemptRef", "successorRef"]` and the other six are assembled from the authenticated principal, the configured project, the envelope correlation, the registry clock and the two contract constants. A payload naming `principalId` is refused whole at PAYLOAD_SHAPE with `INPUT_INVALID`, 400 — never trimmed. The registry's generic `requestOf` could not be reused: it emits `{commandId, correlationId, decidedAt, expectedVersion, kind, payload, principalId, projectId, schemaVersion}`, a shape the exact-key gate rejects.

THE DISPOSITION IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED — the one thing here that could have been a quiet lie. `evaluateContinuationCommandBytes` answers `BOUND` for a first binding AND for an identical retry (continuation-service.ts:86-92 returns the already-durable binding on a REPLAYED commit), and it exposes no disposition. Hard-coding `DECIDED` would have passed the happy-path test and misreported every retry. So the edge reads `readContinuationBindings` BEFORE the call and looks up the returned `bindingRef` in that set; a named test sends the same continuation twice and asserts the second receipt is `REPLAYED`, with the binding count still 1.

TESTS (apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry-continuation.test.ts, 189 lines) — all through `handleCommandRequest` over the PRODUCTION provider, never through the service directly:
- authenticated send -> `{decision:{disposition:"DECIDED", resultCode:"BOUND"}, httpStatus:200, outcome:"ACCEPTED"}`, and the receipt's `effectId` is asserted EQUAL to the `bindingRef` read back out of the store by `readContinuationBindings` — a durable fact, not a returned shape.
- identical retry -> `REPLAYED`, binding count unchanged.
- unauthenticated (`credential: null`) -> `{error:{code:"AUTHENTICATION_FAILED"}, httpStatus:401, stage:"AUTHENTICATE"}`, and no binding was written.
- server fact smuggled (`principalId` in the payload) -> `{error:{code:"INPUT_INVALID"}, httpStatus:400, stage:"PAYLOAD_SHAPE"}`, and no binding was written.
- unreconciled attempt -> `{refusal:{code:"CONTINUATION_ATTEMPT_UNRECONCILED", layer:"CONTINUATION"}, httpStatus:422, stage:"DISPATCH"}`.
- the seed itself is asserted (`expect(seeded.ok).toBe(true)`) before anything uses it.

FIXTURE FACT THE NEXT AGENT WILL WANT. `records(SETTLED)` leaves `safeHandoff: null`, and a continuation over it is refused by the RUNNER with `RECOVERY_RESUME_BOUNDARY_UNPROVEN` at `SAFE_BOUNDARY` — "a resume requires a proven release boundary carrying its exact safe handoff". My first run failed exactly there, and the fixture now seeds `records({ ...SETTLED, safeHandoff: "handoff-1" })`. Worth stating because the refusal is indistinguishable from a broken command edge if you only read the HTTP status: both are 422 PORT_REFUSED. I confirmed the difference with a throwaway probe against `runContinuationCommand` directly, which returned `{"bindingRef":"recovery-continuation:a1:s1","ok":true,"replayed":false,"resultCode":"BOUND"}` once the handoff was present. planningNotes.risks:
1) A DAEMON THAT BOOTS READY AFTER A FAILED SWEEP is the defect, and it is invisible to a verdict-only assertion. Assert the listener is not accepting; drill 2 must redden on READINESS, not on a changed code.
